tagline: South past the spires, where emigrants signed in axle grease.
intro: From Albion, once the county seat and a teachers' college town, Idaho 77 runs south to Connor Creek, where the byway turns off into the gap Cassia Creek cuts between the Cotterell and Jim Sage mountains. Thousands of California Trail emigrants came through that opening. The road follows them on through Elba and Almo to the granite of City of Rocks.

Past Almo the pavement quits. The gravel runs down Birch Creek through a narrow canyon of volcanic cliffs, the old route of the Kelton to Boise stage line, which working ranches use for cattle drives in summer and fall, and comes out at Oakley.
season: Visit Idaho gives April to November as the best weather to travel.

moments.title: Almo
moments.text: Almo keeps a 1938 marker to an 1861 massacre that never happened. The Idaho State Historical Society has recommended taking it down, and the town has refused.

moments.title: City of Rocks National Reserve
moments.text: Emigrants bound for California camped among these granite spires and wrote their names in axle grease on Register Rock, where the signatures can still be read.

moments.title: Oakley
moments.text: The whole town is on the National Register for its century-old stone and brick buildings, and the Howells Opera House dates from 1907.

practical: Between Almo and Oakley the byway is a gravel road.
